skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: Most high-severity static findings are false positives from documentation, placeholders, .gitignore entries, or API key variable names. Confirmed risks are expected outbound MCP network requests, persistent local stats and logs, and an unrestricted MCP configuration path that can launch local commands if mcp-config.json is untrusted. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted MCP command and endpoint configuration
remediation.suggestion: Ship a reviewed mcp-config.json or validate configuration so only the intended Tavily endpoint or command can run. Reject unexpected commands, arguments, environment variables, and hosts.

remediation.issue: Tool arguments are persisted in local logs
remediation.suggestion: Make detailed logging opt in, redact queries and URLs by default, and document how users can delete stats and log files.

remediation.issue: External service receives user queries and URLs
remediation.suggestion: Document exactly what is sent to Tavily or the configured MCP endpoint, and warn users not to submit secrets or private customer data.

remediation.issue: API key diagnostics reveal partial key values
remediation.suggestion: Show only key counts and the last four characters, or hide key previews unless a debug flag is explicitly set.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted MCP Configuration Can Launch Local Commands
semantic_findings.description: executor.py reads mcp-config.json and uses the configured command, args, and env values to create stdio MCP server parameters. If that config is supplied or modified by an untrusted source, the skill can launch arbitrary local commands under the user account.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The executor directly passes config command, args, and env values into StdioServerParameters. The package does not include mcp-config.json, so the intended command or endpoint cannot be verified from the submitted files.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Tool Argument Logging
semantic_findings.description: stats_manager.py records each tool call with its full arguments and appends the record to a local JSONL log file. Search queries, URLs, and research prompts can remain on disk after a session ends.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The call record includes the arguments field and is appended to the logs file. This directly supports the privacy finding.

content.user_title: Search the Web with Tavily MCP
content.value_statement: Agents need current web information, but manual search interrupts research workflows. This skill connects Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to Tavily MCP search tools through a local executor.
actual_capabilities: Calls Tavily MCP tools for search, extraction, crawling, site mapping, and research.
Supports stdio, SSE, and HTTP MCP transports through a local configuration file.
Loads one or more Tavily API keys from a local .env file and rotates them per request.
Provides CLI commands to list tools, describe schemas, call tools, and inspect status.
Tracks local call statistics and recent tool logs for troubleshooting.
limitations: Requires a Tavily API key and a valid mcp-config.json file before it can run.
Sends search queries, URLs, and research prompts to the configured MCP endpoint.
Does not restrict the configured stdio command or HTTP endpoint by default.
Free Tavily accounts may have request limits and result limits.

use_cases.title: Research current topics
use_cases.description: Collect recent web results, source URLs, and summaries for market, policy, or technical research.

use_cases.title: Support coding investigations
use_cases.description: Search for documentation, troubleshooting notes, and recent library behavior while working in an agent session.

use_cases.title: Extract website content
use_cases.description: Retrieve page text, crawl selected sites, and map site structure for knowledge base preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Web Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for recent information about renewable energy storage. Return the top sources with short summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Source Extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the main content from these URLs and summarize the claims, dates, and source names.

prompt_templates.title: Comparative Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare several sources on one topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the latest vector database options for RAG systems. Compare features, pricing signals, and operational tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Site Mapping Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for planning content ingestion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this documentation site, identify the most relevant sections for API onboarding, then recommend pages to extract first.

output_examples.input: Search for recent Kubernetes security guidance.
output_examples.output: A ranked list of sources with titles, URLs, short summaries, and notes about publication date relevance.

output_examples.input: Extract the main content from a product documentation page.
output_examples.output: Clean text or markdown content with the important headings, steps, and source URL preserved.

output_examples.input: Research current AI regulation updates in the United States.
output_examples.output: A concise research brief with source links, key developments, and areas that need human verification.

best_practices: Review mcp-config.json before use and allow only trusted Tavily endpoints or commands.
Store Tavily API keys in the local .env file and keep that file out of version control.
Treat search results as sources to verify, especially for legal, medical, or financial topics.
anti_patterns: Do not send private customer data, secrets, or credentials as search queries.
Do not install an unreviewed mcp-config.json from an unknown source.
Do not rely on free-tier search limits for production or high-volume workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Tavily account?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs a Tavily API key stored in a local .env file.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What Tavily actions are exposed?
faq.answer: It documents search, extract, crawl, map, and research tools through Tavily MCP.

faq.question: Where does the skill store usage data?
faq.answer: It writes local statistics and logs in the skill directory when stats tracking is enabled.

faq.question: Can it run without network access?
faq.answer: No. The search, extraction, crawl, map, and research features require the configured Tavily MCP endpoint.

faq.question: What should I review before installing it?
faq.answer: Review the .env handling, local logging behavior, and mcp-config.json command or endpoint settings.
